subject.title: Update 2026.3.24 silently drops config when HOME changes

question: When an updater runs under a different HOME than the existing Linux systemd gateway service, should OpenClaw preserve the old service root, block and ask for explicit migration, or automatically migrate config/state into the new root?
rationale: The implementation choice affects credential-bearing config, Unix user boundaries, and existing hardening that intentionally drops stale service HOME and OPENCLAW_* values on reinstall.

options.title: Block on cross-HOME mismatch
options.body: Detect the old service root before rewriting and fail closed with a doctor/reinstall migration path unless the operator explicitly opts into migration.

options.title: Preserve prior service root automatically
options.body: Keep the existing service HOME/config/state when it can be read safely, accepting more compatibility but more risk of reusing stale service env.

options.title: Defer to broader systemd migration PR
options.body: Wait for a refreshed systemd managed-env PR to settle service-root and drop-in migration behavior together.

recommendation.title: Block on cross-HOME mismatch
recommendation.body: Detect the old service root before rewriting and fail closed with a doctor/reinstall migration path unless the operator explicitly opts into migration.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has recent central history on package-update restart behavior and is the best available owner for the update/service decision.
